title: Metaphysics of Sound: In Search of Name and Infinity
author: Nadja Furlan Štante and Mateja Kurir
target_audience: Readers interested in metaphysical or interdisciplinary explorations of sound
core_themes: The metaphysical and ontological dimensions of sound
The relationship between sound, language, name, and identity
Infinity as it relates to sound and vibration
The intersections of science, philosophy, and spirituality
The symbolic and experiential understanding of sound
primary_purpose: To explore the metaphysical nature of sound, how it relates to naming, language, and infinity, and to synthesize scientific, philosophical, and spiritual perspectives on the importance and essence of sound in reality.

structure_format.organization: Structured in thematic chapters combining philosophical argument, scientific findings, and spiritual insights
features: Use of historical and contemporary case studies

key_concepts_lessons: Sound is not only a physical phenomenon but also carries deep metaphysical and symbolic significance.
Naming is intertwined with the act of creation and carries both ontological and spiritual weight.
Infinity and limitlessness are accessible through the vibrations and processes of sound.
Language emerges from sound and is foundational to identity, communication, and reality-making.
The study of sound forms a bridge between material reality and transcendental/spiritual experience.
notable_features: Engages with both Western and non-Western traditions
Examines sound beyond acoustics—into the realms of meaning and existence
Original synthesis of ancient and contemporary thought
cultural_historical_context: Written in the early 21st century during renewed scholarly interest in intersections between science and spirituality, as well as the philosophical investigation of sensory phenomena and language.
reception_impact: Appreciated for innovative approach to sound studies
Resonates with academic readers interested in metaphysics and philosophy of language
Considered dense but rewarding by those seeking a deep and nuanced study
Not widely mainstream but noted in interdisciplinary circles
comparable_titles: The Mysticism of Sound and Music by Hazrat Inayat Khan
The Audible Past: Cultural Origins of Sound Reproduction by Jonathan Sterne
Philosophy of Sound Art by Christoph Cox and Daniel Warner
Sound and Sentiment by Steven Feld
